claim_text: An outside party got into PLAID's KARTE service without authorisation, and ZOZO customer data held there leaked
summary: ZOZO says PLAID, which runs the external service KARTE, reported unauthorised access by a third party, and that some customer data ZOZO managed on KARTE leaked. PLAID's own notices confirm the access to KARTE and date it to Nov 13.
detail: Two separate companies' own notices (ZOZO and PLAID) state the access. Nikkei and CNET Japan relay ZOZO's notice, so for sourcing they count as one source behind it. ZOZO's notice describes data it kept on the KARTE service; it does not say ZOZO's own systems were breached.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ZOZO (Tier 1) and PLAID (Tier 1) each state the access; Nikkei and CNET Japan repeat ZOZO's notice.

claim_text: PLAID detected the intrusion on Nov 13; ZOZO cut its data link to KARTE that day; PLAID's probe showed ZOZO's data had leaked by Nov 15
summary: PLAID says it detected the access at 8:59 AM JST on Nov 13 and had blocked the attacker by about 3:23 PM. ZOZO says PLAID told it that day, it cut the data link at once, and PLAID found on Nov 15 that ZOZO's data had leaked.
detail: PLAID says it revoked the stolen credentials, began stopping servers from about 2:27 PM and switched KARTE off for all customers on Nov 13. The times are from its Nov 16 notice. ZOZO published its own notice on Nov 20.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ZOZO's notice gives the Nov 13 and Nov 15 dates; PLAID's notice gives the detection time and containment steps; Nikkei and CNET Japan repeat ZOZO.

claim_text: About 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN users, including former members, had member ID, age, gender and postal code leaked; about 47,000 also had display name, email and phone number
summary: ZOZO lists about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers (former members too) with member ID, age, gender and postal code leaked. About 47,000 more also had display name, email and phone number leaked.
detail: ZOZO says the exact items differ person to person, and any one or several of the listed items may apply. The member ID is an internal management number, not a login. The display name is not a login either. Nikkei and CNET Japan repeat the main figures.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ZOZO's notice gives the counts and fields; Nikkei and CNET Japan repeat them.

claim_text: About 13.93 million WEAR by ZOZO users had member ID, age and gender leaked
summary: ZOZO's notice lists about 13,930,000 users of its WEAR styling app whose member ID, age and gender leaked.
detail: The notice does not say how many people are in both the WEAR and ZOZOTOWN groups, so the two numbers should not be added together.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ZOZO's notice gives the count and fields; Nikkei and CNET Japan repeat it.

claim_text: About 24,000 current and former staff of brands selling on ZOZOTOWN had member ID, company name and name leaked
summary: ZOZO's notice lists about 24,000 current and former contacts at brands that sell on ZOZOTOWN, with member ID, company name and name leaked.
detail: ZOZO says it will contact affected customers and brand staff individually.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ZOZO's notice gives the count and fields; Nikkei and CNET Japan repeat it.

summary: ZOZO's notice says passwords are not managed on KARTE and are not part of the leak.
detail: This is ZOZO's own statement about what it keeps on the service. CNET Japan repeats it. No outside check has been published.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ZOZO's notice states it; CNET Japan repeats it.

claim_text: No credit card leak has been found so far
summary: ZOZO says leaks of credit card information have not been confirmed as of its Nov 20 notice.
detail: The notice words it as 'not confirmed at this time', not as proof none leaked. PLAID is still working through what else was on KARTE and ZOZO says it will announce anything new.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Company's own snapshot as of Nov 20; it cannot be checked from outside and may change.

claim_text: No secondary harm from the leak was known as of Nov 20, per ZOZO, which warns of fake emails, texts and calls
summary: ZOZO says no secondary harm had been confirmed. It warns of suspicious emails, SMS or calls posing as ZOZO and asks people not to open links or attachments. It says it never asks for passwords or card details by email.
detail: Nikkei repeats the 'no secondary harm confirmed' line. This is a snapshot from the company, not a finding that none will occur.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both give the company's own statement as of Nov 20.

claim_text: How the attacker got in: PLAID says they used a flaw in an internal process on a public-facing route to take data, then used stolen credentials to reach KARTE's admin console
summary: PLAID says that on Nov 13 a third party tried several routes and exploited a weakness in internal handling on a publicly reachable path. That let them take data and credentials, which they then used to reach the KARTE admin screen.
detail: This is the vendor's own account of its own breach. No outside forensic report has been published. PLAID says it plans an external security investigation and third-party verification and will publish prevention measures from the results. The notice does not name the flaw.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: PLAID's own notices (Tier 1) give the method; it is one company's account of its own incident, with independent review still pending.

claim_text: Who is behind the PLAID KARTE attack
summary: Neither ZOZO, PLAID, Nikkei nor CNET Japan names an attacker or a claim of responsibility.
detail: PLAID says it is reporting to Japan's personal information protection regulator and consulting police. We did not look at leak sites or forums for claims, and would cite such claims only through press.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the five sources names an attacker.

claim_text: The same KARTE intrusion hit many other companies, not only ZOZO
summary: PLAID's Nov 20 notice counts companies hit in four data groups: 570, 487, up to 409 and 754. A company can be in more than one group. PLAID does not name them.
detail: PLAID does not name the companies. It says some were former customers whose data should have been deleted after their contracts ended but was kept because of human operation and management failures. Nothing in the notices says that applies to ZOZO.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: PLAID's own notice (Tier 1) gives the company counts.

claim_text: KARTE is expected to restart in stages from mid-January 2027
summary: PLAID says all KARTE services have been stopped since Nov 13 and sets a staged restart target of mid-January 2027, after rebuilding parts of the system and an outside check.
detail: This is a plan, not a completed step. PLAID says it will not bill customers for the stopped period and will hand affected companies detailed data from Nov 24.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: PLAID's notice states the plan; it may change.
